gao-gaoreports-gao-08-210g:
Audit standards get a companion tool in GAO publication GAO-08-210G, released December 31, 2007. Government Auditing Standards guide audits of public bodies across the country. GAO revised those standards in July 2007. Auditors must sort which duties in the text bind them and which they should follow. The tool exists to make that sorting plain.

The document maps the professional requirements in the revision. It flags each one by the force of its wording, must or should. It is supplementary to the standards themselves, not a replacement. Audit shops can use it to build checklists and train staff. The tool helps turn a dense rulebook into working steps.
uslaw-usc-t2-s190g:
Section 190g of Title 2 of the United States Code bars consideration of certain private bills in Congress. Title 2 covers Congress, and this section sits in the chapter on congressional procedure and investigations. The hosted text is the version current in twenty twenty six. Private bills seek relief for named persons rather than general law.

No private bill or resolution, including omnibus claims or pension bills, may be considered if it directs payment in barred classes. Amendments to other bills that do the same are also barred. The first barred class covers payment for property damage or for personal injury or death where suit may be brought. The rule channels such claims to courts instead.
